request: Which animal is deadliest to humans? #interactive

sources.title: The Deadliest Animal in the World
sources.finding: mosquitoes kill about 725,000 people a year

commands.speak: Which animal kills the most people? What we fear and what actually kills us turn out to be very different things. Here are four suspects.

ask.question: Rank them: which kills the most people each year? Drag the cards, then press Answer.
ask.right: You got {r}. The smallest one tops the list.
ask.wrong: You got {r}. The real order runs mosquito, snake, dog, and shark last by far.

commands.speak: Let's count. Each bar will be how many people one kind of animal kills in a year, in thousands.
Sharks, the villains of a hundred films: about ten people a year. The bar barely leaves the floor.
Hippos kill around five hundred, crocodiles about a thousand. Huge, fierce, and still almost invisible here.
Dogs: about twenty-five thousand a year.
Snakes: around fifty thousand, mostly farmers bitten far from any hospital with antivenom.

ask.question: Now the mosquito. How many thousand people does it kill a year? Drag its bar to your guess.
ask.right: Close: you said {g} thousand, and it is about {g.true} thousand.
ask.wrong: You said {g} thousand; it is about {g.true} thousand. Most people guess far lower.

commands.speak: Seven hundred and twenty-five thousand. One small insect outkills every predator on this chart, many times over.
Yet the bite itself is harmless. What kills is a parasite, malaria, slipped into your blood with the mosquito's saliva as it drinks.
And the dogs? Mostly not their teeth: rabies, a virus passed in a bite, and almost always fatal once symptoms begin.
So let's sort the killers by how they kill.
Five animals, two ways to kill: by attacking you, or by the germs they carry.

ask.question: Sort them: drag each animal into its box.
ask.right: You got {k}. Snakes and crocodiles attack; the rest kill through germs.
ask.wrong: You got {k}. The tsetse fly carries sleeping sickness, and dogs carry rabies.

commands.speak: That is the pattern: the deadliest animals are not the strongest, but the ones that carry disease from person to person.
One bar is still missing — the runner-up.
Us. Humans kill around four hundred and seventy-five thousand other humans a year, in murders and wars.
So fear sharks if you must. But the animal worth fighting is the one you swat, which is why bed nets and malaria drugs save more lives than any shark net.

quiz.question: Why are mosquitoes so deadly?
quiz.right: They carry the malaria parasite: the bite is harmless, the passenger is not.
